newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn ends mostly up, USDA acreage boosts Dec.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn ends mostly up, USDA acreage boosts Dec.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed mostly higher with a bullish acreage report from USDA allowing new crop December a bit of leeway to the upside, traders said.
USDA Monday said U.S. farmers this year seeded 80.2 million acres to corn, below an average of analysts' estimates for 81.8 million.

"Bean acres were up and corn was down because it is more expensive to produce corn," said Dick Loewy, president of Chicago-based analytical firm AgResource, Inc. "We were mesmerized this spring by early plantings but we should have seen this coming."
USDA said U.S. farmers seeded 70.9 million acres to soybeans, above average expectations for 68.4 million.
But nearly perfect crop weather in the U.S. limited gains in December corn. Also, nearby July, while closing firm, was held in check by the government's quarterly stocks report.
USDA Monday said U.S. corn stocks as of June 1 totalled 2.49 billion bushels, above expectations for 2.478 billion.
A collapse in soybean futures also limited gains in corn.
Corn closed four cents per bushel higher to 1-1/2 cents lower, with July up 1-3/4 at $2.48 a bushel. December closed 2-3/4 higher at $2.38-1/4.

Bearish input also came from Friday's USDA Hogs and Pigs report which showed the U.S. hog herd was not expanding as fast as expected. That scenario will trim the amount of corn expected to be consumed.

USDA's weekly export inspections report was mildly supportive. USDA said during the week ended June 26 corn inspected for export totalled 28.9 million bushels, near the high end of expectations for 24 million to 29 million bushels.

A new contract low was set early in nearby July of $2.40 per bushel, below the previous low of $2.45-1/2 set Friday. Also, a fresh two-year low was set in the July as the contract reached the lowest level for a nearby since March 1995.
In late dealings, Dean Witter bought 1.5 million bushels of December and Produce Grain bought one million December, traders said.

On the day, Rosenthal Collins bought seven million bushels of December, Tenco Inc bought 4.5 million December and Dean Witter bought two million bushels of December, traders said. Refco Inc sold nine million bushels of December, traders said.
In spread trading, Griffin Trading did nine million bushels of September/July at eight cents, premium July and spread four million bushels of December/July, traders said.
Corn futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 100,000 contracts, above the 96,769 traded Friday.

In corn options, ABN Amro-Chicago Corp bought 1,600 December $2.20 puts at 3-3/4 to four cents and sold 700 December $2.80 puts at 46 to 48 cents, traders said. FIMAT Futures bought 2,500 December $2.70 calls at 3-7/8 to 4-1/2 cents, traders said.
Corn options volume was estimated at 25,000 contracts, below the 33,569 traded Friday.
